title: Escalation standby checklist + war-room prep (Rowan)
content:
Purpose: quick personal standby notes for a customer-facing war-room. Not a canonical runbook — my rapid checklist when I’m first on call or asked to spin up a war-room.

Top-level goals:
- Contain impact (who sees degraded responses / errors)
- Give customer clear, frequent status updates (raise confidence)
- Stabilize traffic (switch routing / reduce load)
- Triage root cause or safe fallback (model rollback, regional routing)

Pre-call quick gathers (first 5-10m):
- Confirm customer and scope: customer-xyz, region eu-west1, product: search-summaries pipeline
- Incident timeline: when did errors start? last successful deploy?
- Metrics to pull: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, token cost spike, request QPS by route, errors by model variant, kv cache hit rate
- Dashboards to open: Console -> model-usage (route: /v1/generate), infra -> dedicated-pool-eu-west1, logs -> logging.query (errors)
- Check recent changes: commits/rollouts in last 24h (GH PRs + config changes), infra events (reboots, autoscaler), capacity adjustments
- SLOs to reference: latency p95 <= 600ms, error rate <= 0.5% (customer SLA: 99.7 availability)

Roles (assign immediately):
- War-room lead: Rowan (me) -> coordinates communications and decisions
- Eng on-call (serving-runtime): Omar Rivera -> infra & worker troubleshooting
- Model owner / applied-ml: Asha Nair -> model behavior / rollout decisions
- Customer Success (CS): Priya Singh (if available) -> customer comms and liaison
- Scribe: auto-make a Google doc and capture timestamps / decisions

Immediate comms templates (short & copy-paste):
- Slack to #cust-xyz-incident: "Standup: War-room created for customer-xyz outage (eu-west1). Primary impact: increased 5xx and slow p95 on /v1/generate. Standby team: Rowan, Omar, Asha. Next update in 10m. If you have logs or recent deploy links drop here."
- Customer email/status (first contact): "We’re actively investigating elevated errors and increased latency on your eu-west1 traffic. Engineering is in a war-room and we will provide an update every 15 minutes. Immediate mitigations being evaluated: routing to fallback variant and scaling dedicated capacity. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you posted."

Decision gates (what triggers what):
- If error rate > 1.5% for 5m -> consider routing to fallback model variant (A/B fallback)
- If p95 > 1200ms and latency trend worsening -> enable autoscale burst to +30% capacity
- If errors tied to specific model version (errors by variant > 90% concentrated) -> rollback to previous pinned model version

Quick mitigations checklist (try in parallel where safe):
- [ ] Verify routing policy: are requests being routed to the intended pool? (console/routing)
- [ ] Pin traffic to previous stable model version (rollback option)
- [ ] Flip to lower-capacity but more stable variant (fallback)
- [ ] Increase dedicated pool nodes (burst) if autoscaler lagging
- [ ] Temporarily disable batching or reduce batch_size to reduce latencies
- [ ] Clear prefix/KV cache if corrupted (careful: invalidates perf gains)
- [ ] If memory OOMs observed: restart affected worker pods and monitor for restarts count

Useful quick queries / commands (copyable):
- PromQL (errors): sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=serving,code=~"5..",customer="customer-xyz"}[1m])) by (instance)
- Latency p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{customer="customer-xyz"}[5m])) by (le))
- Recent deploys: gh api repos/redwood-inference/deploys --query 'deploys[?created_at>=`2026-02-28`]' (or check console deploy history)

What to capture during war-room (scribe checklist):
- Timestamps of each decision and who approved it
- Exact config changes (model id, version, routing change ids)
- Any customer-visible messages and time sent
- Link to logs/trace for the moment of degradation (span ids)

Short-term follow-ups (post-meeting action items):
- Rowan: create incident doc stub (add timeline + initial mitigation steps) — ETA: +2h
- Omar: collect worker logs and memory profiles, upload to incident doc — ETA: +1h
- Asha: run quick eval on fallback variant for quality regressions (sample batch) — ETA: +1.5h
- Priya: draft customer status update and confirm send time with CS/Eng — ETA: +30m

Open questions (call these out early):
- Is this traffic spike organic or test traffic from customer QA (recent deploy)?
- Any config push from customer's side (api key rotation, changed prompt) that could cause malformed requests?
- Did autoscaler contract recently change (min nodes high/low) that prevented scale-up?

Post-incident/After-action (notes for postmortem):
- Timeline with exact metrics at each decision point (+ graphs)
- Root cause hypothesis and confidence level (evidence: logs/traces)
- Suggested platform changes: better autoscale lead time, pre-warming, stronger routing fallback defaults, alert tuning (thresholds for error rate)
- Customer follow-up: detailed RCA + mitigation steps + preventive commitments (who signs off)

Personal reminders / heuristics (my shorthand):
- Keep updates short and metric-backed (no speculation)
- If customer is panicked, reduce cadence to every 10m but be conservative in what you promise
- Prefer rollback to an earlier model over aggressive config hacks unless evidence points to transient infra issue

Notes-to-self TODOs:
- Add this checklist to my personal quick-reference war-room doc (~link)
- Propose a lightweight template to product for true-automatic fallback routing (Asha + Prod PM)

End-of-file: quick template for the final customer post-incident note: 
"Thanks for your patience — we identified that [root cause summary]. Immediate mitigations: [list]. We will do [next steps] and follow up with an RCA within 3 business days. If you’d like a 1:1 walkthrough of the incident, we can schedule it."

-- Rowan
